title: v1/chat.completions: tolerant stop-weighting + streaming functioncall stabilization
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Enhances /v1/chat.completions parity: introduces configurable stop token weighting to better match OpenAI semantics, reduces false premature termination in streaming with function/tool calling, and wraps structured JSON responses with stricter envelope validation. Backwards compatible by default.
description:
Motivation: Several customers surfaced subtle differences between Redwood's chat v1 adapter and OpenAI's /v1/chat.completions around (1) how we treat multiple stop sequences when decisions are ambiguous mid-stream, and (2) edge cases where a streaming functioncall path would emit partial tool output and then close the stream causing callers to see invalid JSON. This change introduces a stop-weighting mechanism (configurable, opt-in for now) that biases candidate stop matches based on token alignment heuristics, and hardens the streaming functioncall handshake so partial tool output is buffered and re-framed into the structured JSON envelope expected by OpenAI clients.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a stop-weighting layer in the chat param translator to reconcile multiple stop specs and prefer the longest/earliest-weighted candidate in parity with OpenAI heuristics.
- Implements a streaming stabilizer that buffers function/toolcall fragments until a complete framed JSON object or safe flush boundary is seen; this prevents truncated JSON being delivered to SDKs.
- Normalizes logprobs emitted during stop events so token probability attribution mirrors OpenAI's reported token slices (adjusts KV-cache flush timing during stop handling).
- Adds structured envelope validation with a recovery path that attempts a best-effort JSON merge for near-complete fragments (experimental, behind the feature flag).
- Exposes a new map of 2 config knobs: chatv1.stop_weight_mode ("off"|"len_bias"|"prob_bias") and streaming.tool_buffer_ms (integer, default 50ms) that customers can set per-route.

Compatibility notes: Default behavior is unchanged (stop_weight_mode=off). When teams opt into len_bias/prob_bias, some legacy prompts that relied on shortest-stop precedence may see different cut points — these are deliberate to match OpenAI parity in our internal evals. The streaming tool buffering is safe and defaulted to 50ms; we did not observe measurable latency regression in our canary tests for common seq lengths.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for the stop-weight matcher with 120+ crafted cases covering overlapping stops, multi-byte tokens, and role-prefixed stop sequences.
- Integration tests that spin up the chat v1 adapter + runtime streamer and run scripted toolcall sessions with deliberately fragmented outputs.
- E2E compatibility harness that compares Redwood vs OpenAI responses on 500 prompt/toolcall pairs (pass threshold: 95% parity on stop placement, 99% JSON validity).
- Canary rollout to perf-lab and 3 beta customers for 72h; telemetry shows 0.4% increase in average token latency for small responses and no increase in error-rate.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind chatv1.experimental.stop_weighting; initial rollout via per-customer config in console with a 2-week canary followed by global opt-in default. If metrics regress >1% error-rate or JSON-MALFORMED anomalies appear, the flag will be auto-reverted.

Related work: ENG-9876 implements a related KV-cache timing fix that reduced misaligned logprobs; PM-3321 requested a customer-facing knob for stop behavior. SUP-412 tracks a customer incident that motivated the streaming JSON hardening.
